full_judgment: 4. The defendant-opposite parties contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint, contending, inter-alia, that the schedule to the plaint is indefinite and unspecified; the plaintiff-petitioner has no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and also stated that there is no existence of Samity named কালীগড় ব্যবসার সম্পদ লিমিটেড and the alleged Sachna Bazar Banik Samity has/had no right to lease out the suit land to the plaintiff's father. Further case of the defendant-opposite parties, is that, the property in question belongs to nobody and there is no owner and claimant of the suit property. For that reason the property in question is liable to be made khas under section 19(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and accordingly, the Government is taking step for making the property khas to the government. The plaintiff being informed about the said process of the Government, for illegal gain and to grab the property filed the suit against the defendants with false allegation of giving threat to the plaintiff. The plaintiff has got no cause of action against the defendants to file the suit for permanent injunction and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
